reports.headline: Friday the 6th in Spain: Daniel Monzón's “Ruega por nosotras”, “Fiesta Pagäna” and “Godzilla Minus Zero” lead 14 releases
reports.deck: Sensacine counts fourteen titles for 6 November, including a drama about Franco-era reformatories, the Mägo de Oz biopic and Japan's Godzilla sequel.
paragraphs: According to Sensacine's calendar, fourteen titles reach Spanish cinemas on Friday 6 November. The ones that stand out for us are “Ruega por nosotras”, “Fiesta Pagäna” and “Godzilla Minus Zero”; we mentioned “Sacamantecas” a few days ago.

“Ruega por nosotras” is Daniel Monzón's new drama, co-written with Jorge Guerricaechevarría. Per Guía del Ocio, it is set in 1974: a 19-year-old from a wealthy Barcelona family is sent to a strict reformatory in Madrid, inspired by Franco's Patronato de Protección a la Mujer, and befriends Sole and other girls. Zoe Bonafonte and Manuela Calle (in her film debut) star. It was shown at San Sebastián, out of competition. A period film with a social eye; we haven't seen it.

“Fiesta Pagäna”, by Álvaro Brechner, is the biopic of folk-metal band Mägo de Oz, with Adrián Lastra and Roberto Álamo. It premiered at the Morelia festival on 22 October and arrives with controversy: some voices from the band oppose it and legal action was taken against the producer, per a Mexican outlet; we found no current status. “Godzilla Minus Zero” is Takashi Yamazaki's sequel, set two years after the first film; Espinof gives 6 November in its body text and the 9th in its subtitle, so we rely on Sensacine's calendar date.

Lee Chang-dong's “Possible Love” (“Un amor posible”) also appears on Sensacine's calendar for the 6th, the day it hits Netflix; Cinemanía, however, says 23 October, and Netflix's note only lists cinemas in South Korea, Australia, the US, Canada, the UK, Ireland and Japan. We don't assume a Spanish cinema release: check local listings.

reports.headline: November Fridays in Spain: McDonagh, Ti West, Nemes's “Moulin”, “The Hunger Games” and Ione Hernández's “Hermanas”
reports.deck: A look at the titles Sensacine schedules for the 13th, 20th and 27th; calendar data only, with no reviews or verified synopses.
paragraphs: According to Sensacine's calendar, Friday the 13th brings, among others, Martin McDonagh's “Wild Horse Nine”; Ti West's “Scrooge y los fantasmas de la Navidad”; Zachary Wigon's “Victorian Psycho”; David Leitch's “Cómo robar un banco” and Isaki Lacuesta's “Jaleos”.

On Friday the 20th the list includes Francis Lawrence's “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” (“Amanecer en la cosecha”); László Nemes's “Moulin”; Jane Schoenbrun's “Adolescencia, sexo y muerte en Campamento Miasma”, and Gemma Ferraté's “Citas: La película”. On the 27th: Ione Hernández's “Hermanas”, Dani de la Orden's “El director” and Marion Le Corroller's “Sanguine”, which lands on the 27th here, not the 6th as we doubted days ago.
This is a preview only. It rests on a single calendar: we will check each Friday with the distributors, and we haven't verified synopses or casts for these titles.

reports.headline: OperaVision: “Le Roi d'Ys” shows “last chance”, and the platform lists “Šárka” and “Peter Grimes” for November
reports.deck: Three more productions from the May lineup would also expire this month, per OperaWire; OperaVision's own site doesn't confirm it.
paragraphs: OperaVision, the free online opera platform, marks “Le Roi d'Ys” from the Opéra national du Rhin as “last chance”. Per OperaWire, Oliver Py's production, conducted by Samy Rachid, went up on 8 May and expires on 8 November; the recording dates from March this year.

OperaWire gives three further expiries, six months after release: Iain Bell's “Medusa” at La Monnaie (15 November), the Hungarian State Opera's “Così fan tutte” (23) and Ponchielli's “I Lituani” from Vilnius (29). We did not find those three on OperaVision's front page, so check before counting on them.

Among new releases, the site announces “De Materie” (6 November), “Šárka” from the National Theatre Brno (15) and “Peter Grimes” from the Finnish National Opera (26). There is also the International Opera Awards gala (21) and two children's and family titles on the 22nd. These dates come from OperaVision's schedule; we haven't verified casts or subtitles, and the platform doesn't say how long they stay up.

reports.headline: Calendar: Tokyo closes today, fourteen releases on Friday the 6th, and “Le Roi d'Ys” expires on Sunday the 8th
reports.deck: Outlook to 15 November and key dates this month, keeping Spain apart from other countries.
paragraphs: This week. Wednesday 4: the Tokyo festival closes, and we haven't yet found the winners. Friday 6, in Spain: fourteen releases per Sensacine (“Ruega por nosotras”, “Fiesta Pagäna”, “Godzilla Minus Zero”, “Sacamantecas”), “Possible Love” on Netflix and “De Materie” on OperaVision. Sunday 8: “Le Roi d'Ys” expires on OperaVision.

Later. Friday 13, in Spain: McDonagh, Ti West and David Leitch. Sunday 15: “Šárka” arrives on OperaVision and “Medusa” expires (per OperaWire). Friday 20: “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” and “Moulin”. Saturday 21: International Opera Awards gala. Thursday 26: “Peter Grimes” on OperaVision. Friday 27: “Sanguine” and “Hermanas”. All release dates are for Spain, per Sensacine.

reports.headline: Editor's picks: “Possible Love”, “Ruega por nosotras” and “Le Roi d'Ys” before it expires
reports.deck: Three suggestions with editorial affinity (not a critics' score) and confidence, plus the day's wrap-up.
paragraphs: “Possible Love” (2026): affinity 4 out of 5, medium confidence. Lee Chang-dong returns eight years after “Burning” with a 164-minute drama that won at Venice, per Cinemanía; on Netflix on 6 November. We haven't seen it.

“Ruega por nosotras” (2026): affinity 3 out of 5, low confidence. A period drama about Franco-era reformatories by Daniel Monzón; we only know the synopsis and credits. “Le Roi d'Ys” (2026, OperaVision): affinity 3 out of 5, low confidence; it's free and expires on 8 November, but we have no full cast.

Day's wrap-up. A day of releases rather than news: Spain has fourteen titles on Friday, Tokyo closes without winners in hand, and there's one opera production to see soon. We dropped items from sources we couldn't read.
